notes.title: Alpha 0.2.1 update
notes.content:
Hello everybody, we got a minor update today including:

[list]
[*] for those of you who want more precision - sensitivity slider for each axis in control customization panel
[*] for our VR streamers - fullscreen wide 16:9 mirror mode
[*] for our VR players - visible motion controllers in-game with controls mapping drawn over them, you can turn them off in VR menu 
[*] we also fixed page switching in options menu with MC, you can switch pages with left/right grip buttons
[*] Panther "wheels" visuals! ːsteamhappyː
[*] bunch of small fixes
[/list]

GLHF and see you in 2017,
PeopleGottaPlay team

notes.title: Thick Air Alpha 0.2 is finally here!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26215335/90dc7f1e209a255502f7b7f3eaa01a03b7ccb470.png[/img]

It took much longer than anyone expected but the scale is so huge it was totally worth the wait. All in all, it feels like a completely different game now, so let's recap what have changed.

First and foremost, 
[h1]PERFORMANCE[/h1]
After several rounds of optimization, we've managed in get up to 100% FPS increase in both VR and standard modes. We didn't, however, switch to UE's new forward renderer, so the visuals are the same quality.

[h1]CONTROLS[/h1]
Alpha 0.2 introduces controls customization system and HOTAS support (actually any DirectInput controller). We ditched prebuilt control schemes except for arcade, which is now default - you are free to build your own control scheme in any fashion you like.

We've also added support for Vive motion controllers. You can play using thumbpad or the entire MC as joystick (hold grip button for that), but be warned, as with any other controller that doesn't have a point of reference (zero), it's not precise at all and extremely exhausting for your hands/arms. The recommended control device is gamepad - still.

[h1]GAMEPLAY[/h1]
No more loading, no map in hangar (which should make sitting VR users happy) - just pick a drone and fly out of the hangar. Introducing semi-open world travel - you are free to fly on your own through the canyon (more locations coming later). There are race points scattered in the canyon - fly up close to one to start the race.

Next, we've made all drones a bit faster, AI a bit smarter, and added gates - you won't miss them (pun intended) but if you do, you'll get disqualified. We've made them big enough, don't worry and get your flying skills up.

[h1]EVERYTHING ELSE[/h1]
We've fixed a bunch of small stuff here and there. I hope I'm not forgetting anything important, but if I am, you'll probably find it on your own. As usual, if you happen to find bugs or glitches, tell us about it in the comments here on on community forum.

Oh, and demo will be updated too, once goddamn script kiddies stop messing up Steam - it's full featured, but not full content. You have access to one drone model and one race track, but you are free to fly in the canyon on your own for however long you want.

Cheers, people, and Merry Christmas ːsteamhappyː
Yours truly,
PeopleGottaPlay

notes.title: Important controls update!
notes.content:
We've been able to locate the biggest source of frustration with Thick Air controls - lack of stabilization on turning and maneuvering thrusters. The stabilization has been implemented in the latest update and it does wonders to controllability. [b]Thruster stabilization[/b] is turned on by default and you can turn it off anytime you want from the options menu.

[quote]All credit for steering/maneuvering thrusters stabilization feature goes to /r/gamedev community and specifically to /u/nomnaut for taking the time to test and figure out the source of the problem.[/quote]

Another important part of this update is [b]arcade control scheme[/b] (now set as default) - steering and height controls bound to left stick and pitch/roll to right, but one left stick is more than enough to fly at high speeds and make all the crazy turns.

The update is live right now both for the game and the demo. Tell us what you think!

notes.title: Patch notes for 9/20/2016
notes.content:
We are introducing new flight mechanic - close-to-ground speed up. It makes the race much more dynamic and brings a risk-reward tactic to play - flying low is risky and requires a lot of skill but the speed advantage is invaluable.

Tell us what you think!
